page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton processor family with Neoverse-V1 cores. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz with single-threaded execution per core. Its cache hierarchy features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached EBS volumes for persistent data, and no discrete GPUs are present.

A central architectural differentiator of the c7gn series is its network throughput, offering a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory and network I/O performance. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 248.85 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 106.15 GB/sec, placing the system in the top 25 percent. The PassMark memory test ranks in the top tier at 3130.42. The instance delivers solid multi-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 17673.0 and static web serving throughput of 50.36 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics sit within average ranges, and large language model inference on 70B parameter models exhibits lower throughput due to CPU-bound execution.

From an efficiency perspective, the ARM Neoverse-V1 architecture provides high compute density and energy-efficient throughput per core, making it cost-effective for scaled execution that benefits from linear multi-core scaling. The 100 Gbps baseline networking makes the instance particularly effective for network-intensive and distributed tasks, including high-throughput web serving, network appliances, continuous integration pipelines, microservices, and distributed data processing frameworks.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gn.8xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized virtual machine powered by AWS Neoverse-V1 Graviton processors under the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores, 32 vCPUs clocked at 2.6 GHz, and 64.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without integrated local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier memory subsystem performance, reaching 248.85 GB/sec read and 106.15 GB/sec write bandwidth, alongside strong multi-core Geekbench and web-serving results. The single-thread-per-core configuration prevents hyper-threading resource contention, providing predictable CPU performance. The platform is well-matched for network-intensive compute tasks, high-capacity web serving, distributed analytics, and ARM-native continuous integration workloads.
